blog_summary: The blog post discusses RNNvis, a tool designed to visualize and interpret the inner workings of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), which are often considered 'black boxes' due to their complexity. Adrian Colyer highlights the lack of understanding around how RNNs store and process information in their hidden states, which limits improvements and user trust in these models. RNNvis aims to address this by providing an interactive visualization tool that breaks down the relationships between input words, hidden states, and model outputs. The tool uses techniques like co-clustering and bipartite graph modeling to structure and interpret the high-dimensional hidden state space. Key features include visualizing individual hidden states, their responses to input sequences, and comparing different RNN variants (e.g., vanilla RNN, LSTM, GRU) to understand their behavior. The post emphasizes the potential for such tools to become part of 'Interactive Model Development Environments' (IMDEs) that combine training, visualization, and model management.

figures.title: The interface of RNNVis
figures.caption: The control panel (A) shows parameter settings of an RNN and allows users to adjust visualization style. The main view (B-D) contains glyph-based sentence visualization (B), memory chips visualization for hidden state clusters (C), and word clouds visualization for word clusters (D). The detail view (E) shows the distributions of models responses to selected word “of” and interpretations of selected hidden units.
